source.excerpt: Our job is to love others
trail: Wikiquote credits the sentence to a Merton letter to Dorothy Day, via the 2005 collection Catholic Voices in a World on Fire, p. 180.
John Swinton’s BRF article supplies the more specific reference: Jim Forest, “The spiritual roots of protest,” in Stephen Hand’s edited volume.
The date of the letter is not established by these references; the collection’s 2005 date must not be presented as the composition date.

author.name: Thomas Merton
author.heading: About Thomas Merton
author.bio: Thomas Merton (1915–1968) was a Trappist monk at the Abbey of Gethsemani in Kentucky. His autobiography The Seven Storey Mountain brought him a wide readership; his later writing and correspondence addressed contemplation, racial justice, nonviolence and dialogue across religious traditions.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The line is transmitted as advice in Merton’s correspondence with Dorothy Day. The passage continues by treating worthiness as something love may bring about, rather than a test that must be passed before love is offered. Its surviving quotation context is practical Christian concern for one’s neighbors.
